 Judgment

These appeals under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 are filed challenging the Judgment and award dated 31.10.2017 passed by the VII Addl.SCJ and XXXII ACMM, Member,
MACT-3, Bengaluru in MVC No.4307/2016.

MACT-3,

sentences.text: 2. The claimant filed the claim petition under Section 166 of the MV Act claiming just and proper compensation for having suffered accidental injuries in a road traffic accident on 6.5.2016 due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the car.
3. The Tribunal after appreciating the evidence on record awarded a total compensation of Rs.2,74,400/- with interest at the rate of 8% p.a. from the date of petition till actual realization.

Taking exception to the same, the claimant is in appeal in MFA No.255/2018 seeking enhancement ,
and the Insurance company is in appeal in MFA No.1493/2018 challenging the liability as well as quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

4. Learned counsel for the Insurance company submits that Exs.R.1 to R.4 clearly establishes that the claimant sustained injuries due to the self fall, and the vehicle insured under the policy issued by the Insurance company was falsely implicated by fabricating documents at Ex.P.6. by showing that the claimant was hit by a Car.
He further argues that the compensation awarded to the claimant is exorbitant, and sought for setting aside the impugned award.
Per contra, learned counsel for the claimant submits that although in Ex.R.1 to R.4 it is stated that injuries sustained by the claimant is due to self fall.
However, in Ex.R1 there was an entry made by the ESI hospital that the claimant was admitted as an inpatient due to the injuries sustained in road traffic accident while riding the bike.
The entry made in Exs.R1. to R.4 is based on the statement made by the public who shifted him to the hospital.
6. The Tribunal after considering both oral and documentary evidence and the charge sheet has rightly held that the claimant sustained accidental injuries in a road traffic accident.
He further submits that the compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal is meager and sought for enhancement of compensation.

sentences.text: Considered the arguments of the learned counsel for the parties, and perused the trial Court records.
8. Ex.
P.6 wound certificate indicates that the claimant sustained injuries in a road traffic accident and there is a entry that the claimant was riding his motor cycle when he was hit by a car.
Exs. R.1
to R.4 produced by the Insurance Company reflects that the history of injuries as self fall from the bike.

The Tribunal after considering oral and documentary evidence on record has observed as follows:
"No doubt, Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.4 relied upon by respondent No.1, do mention the history of injuries as self fall or fall from the bike, but as stated above at bottom of Ex.R.1 there is entry which reveals that "patient gives history of RTA hit by Car while riding bike".

In order to contravene the aforesaid documents, the Wound certificate relied NC: 2024:KHC:21444 upon by the petitioner marked at Ex.P.6 issued by the very same hospital i.e., ESI hospital, it is clearly mentioned "hit by a Car while riding two-wheeler".

Even in Ex.P.11 the Inpatient record issued by ESI hospital, there is a mention as "patient gives history of hit by Car while riding bike" along with the signature of the person who has entered said information.

17. Apart from these documents, petitioner as stated above, has examined the charge sheet eye- witness by name B.V.Venkatesh S/o Venkatachalayya, who in his affidavit evidence has reiterated the version of P.W.1 stating that accident occurred due to rash and negligent and high speed of the driver of the Car bearing reg.

This witness has been cross- examined at length by the counsel for respondent No.1, wherein he has deposed that he do not know either petitioner or his father and on the date of accident he was going by bus towards Est Rajajinagar and he started from Nagarabhavi by bus and got down at ESI stop, Rajajinagar and the petitioner was riding two- wheeler in the modera speed and he saw the offending vehicle Car at the tir of accident and himself and public took the petition to nearest ES hospital and he showed the accid spot to the Police and in his presence spot Maha came to be prepared by the Police at the scene occurrence.
Although this witness has been cr examined by the counsel for respondent No.1, nothing worth material has been elicited from him order to disbelieve his version.

9. The findings recorded by the Tribunal is on appreciating the evidence on record, and in the absence of any perversity or illegality in the said findings, the same cannot be said to be suffering from any illegality.
Therefore, the contention of the learned counsel for the Insurance Company that the motor cycle NC: 2024:KHC:21444 covered under the policy issued by it has been falsely implicated is not acceptable.
10. The accident is of the year 2016, and the claimant was aged about 21 years.
In the absence of proof of income, the notional income is assessed at Rs. 9,500/- p m..

The claimant sustained accidental injuries to the left lower limb 1/3rd both bone fracture -closed, and grazed abrasion over left side of the fact over left temporal region 10 cm X 14 cm and over nasal bridge 2cm X 1cm.

sentences.text: The doctor assessed the permanent physical disability at 42% to the left lower limb and 21% to the whole body.
The Tribunal assessed functional disability at 12% instead of 14%.

Therefore, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is reassessed as follows:
 Pain and sufferings Rs.75,000/-
 Loss of amenities, Food, Rs.50,000/-
 nourishment, attendant charges  etc

Medical expenses -  Future medical expenses Rs.15,000/-
 Loss of future income due to Rs. 2,87,218  disability 9,500 X 14% x 12 x 18  Loss of income during the laid Rs.28,500/-
 up period.
 Total Rs.4,55,718/-
 NC: 2024:KHC:21444  12.
Claimant is entitled for the total compensation of Rs.4,55,718/- as against 2,74,400/- awarded by the Tribunal with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till actual realization.
However, the interest at 8% p.a. payable on the compensation is on the higher side.
To this extent, the impugned award stands modified.
13. The appellant - Insurance Company shall pay compensation amount of Rs.4,55,718/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till actual realization.
14. The statutory amount in deposit made before this Court to be transferred to the jurisdictional Tribunal for disbursal to the claimant.
15. The entire compensation amount to be released in favour of the claimant.
Accordingly, the appeals are allowed in part.
